_metadata.source: USDA FNS SNAP Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) States Chart, August 2025 (original sourcing; per-state gross income limits and asset rules taken from this chart at authoring time). A contemporaneous cross-check against the CBPP BBCE page was intended per this field's original wording, but no record exists of that page actually having been fetched at authoring time.
_metadata.source_chart_url_status: dead — returns HTTP 404 as of 2026-08-08, confirmed during the BBCE count re-verification below. Not re-hosted at a known replacement URL; left in place per CONTRIBUTING.md (do not silently drop a citation) rather than deleted.
_metadata.verification_note: Per-state gross income limits and asset rules taken from the USDA FNS BBCE States Chart (last updated August 2025) at authoring time. 46 BBCE jurisdictions (43 states + DC + GU + VI). The 7 non-BBCE states are KS, MS, MO, SD, TN, UT, WY. Gross income limit dollar values are NOT stored here; SNAPBBCESource derives them from us_fpl_{fpl_year}.json using SNAP's published rounding ceil(annual_fpl * pct / 100 / 12).

reverification_2026_08.note: A 2026-08 pass re-verified the 46-jurisdiction count and every per-state gross-income/asset-limit figure in this file, after an internal review flagged that the prose elsewhere in this repo said '45' while this file's own breakdown ('43 states + DC + GU + VI') already summed to 46. Both the FNS chart URL above and the CBPP BBCE page (https://www.cbpp.org/research/food-assistance/snaps-broad-based-categorical-eligibility-supports-working-families-older) were unreachable during this pass (404 and HTTP 403 respectively) — CBPP was NOT actually cross-checked in this pass, despite the 'source' field's original wording implying otherwise.
reverification_2026_08.corroborating_source_used: FRAC 'Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility' one-pager, https://frac.org/wp-content/uploads/Broad-Based-Categorical-Eligibility.pdf, which cites and mirrors the USDA FNA chart at https://www.fna.usda.gov/snap/broad-based-categorical-eligibility (accessed by FRAC June 2026). It lists the same 46 jurisdictions with matching per-state gross-income percentages and asset limits, including idiosyncratic cases (Iowa 160%, Nebraska $25,000 liquid-asset cap, Texas $5,000 cap excluding one vehicle, Guam 165%, Virgin Islands 175%, the Arkansas elderly/non-elderly two-tier split, the New York dependent-care/earned-income two-tier split), and confirms KS/MS/MO/SD/TN/UT/WY are absent from the BBCE table.
reverification_2026_08.count_history: USDA's State Options Report, 17th Edition (data reference October 2024) shows 44 BBCE states + 9 non-BBCE (53 total incl. DC/GU/VI) as of that reference date — 2 fewer BBCE jurisdictions than this file's 46. The delta traces to two adoptions after October 2024: Alaska via HB 344 (effective 2025-07-01) and Arkansas via Act 675 (a narrow adoption that retains the $5,500 asset cap, consistent with the AR row in this file). Both match this file's AK and AR rows and account fully for the 44-to-46 change; no jurisdiction in this file is misclassified.
reverification_2026_08.verification_status: verified — 46-jurisdiction count and per-state figures corroborated against FRAC's FNS-sourced mirror and the USDA State Options Report 17th Edition + AK/AR statute citations; NOT independently cross-checked against CBPP or the original FNS chart PDF in this pass, both of which were unreachable.

modeling_notes: net_income_test_applies is true for every jurisdiction. CBPP notes BBCE technically permits states to raise or eliminate the net income limit, but in practice the 100% FPL net test is near-universally applied. Treated here as a modeling assumption. (This modeling assumption traces to the original Aug 2025 authoring; it was not re-derived from CBPP in the 2026-08 re-verification pass, which could not reach the CBPP page — see reverification_2026_08.)

asset_limit: null = asset/resource test fully waived; a number = state-imposed liquid-asset cap; non-BBCE states carry 3000 (the federal general limit, distinct from the 4500 elderly/disabled limit which is not encoded per-row).
Two-tier states encode the broader (headline) tier; the second tier is recorded in second_tier.
BBCE is conferred by receipt of a non-cash TANF/MOE-funded benefit or service (e.g. an informational brochure, referral, or 1-800 number), not by cash assistance.

federal_default.source_note: Federal SNAP rules: 130% FPL gross, 100% FPL net, $3,000 general / $4,500 elderly-disabled asset limit (7 CFR 273.8, 273.9).
